title: A1.1 Lektion 1 · Hallo! Ich bin Nicole … · part 2

steps.title: Greetings, how are you, and spelling your name
steps.body:
**Greetings depend on the time of day:**

- *Guten Morgen* until about 10–11 am · *Guten Tag* during the day (formal) · *Guten Abend* from about 6 pm · *Gute Nacht* only when going to bed
- *Hallo* is informal, any time. In northern Germany you'll also hear *Moin* all day.
- Leaving: *Tschüs* (informal) · *Auf Wiedersehen* (formal) · on the phone *Auf Wiederhören*

**How are you?** There are three versions:

- *Wie geht's?* (short, everyday)
- *Wie geht es dir?* (to a *du* person)
- *Wie geht es Ihnen?* (to a *Sie* person)

Answers: *Sehr gut, danke.* · *Gut, danke.* · *Es geht.* (so-so) · *Nicht so gut.* Then return the question: *Und dir? / Und Ihnen?*

**Spelling** (*buchstabieren*) comes up all the time at offices and on the phone: *Wie schreibt man das?* → *Ich buchstabiere: F-A-R-H-A-N.* The vowels sound different from English: **A** = "ah", **E** = "eh", **I** = "ee", **J** = "yot", **V** = "fow", **W** = "vay", **Z** = "tset". Umlauts are spelled *A-Umlaut* etc., and ß is *Eszett*.

words.example: Guten Tag, ich habe einen Termin.
Guten Abend! Wie geht es Ihnen?

steps.title: Kursbuch p. 11–12 and Arbeitsbuch Lektion 1
steps.body:
**Kursbuch:**

- **p. 11, exercise 7:** listen again and fill in the gaps (*Lektion 1, 7*).
- **p. 11, exercise 8:** listen (*Lektion 1, 8*) and match the answers to *Wie geht's?*
- **p. 12, Sprechtraining 9:** listen to the alphabet (*Lektion 1, 9a*), repeat it, then spell your full name out loud twice.
- **p. 12, exercise 10:** listen (*Lektion 1, 10*) and match the greetings to the pictures.
- Read the grammar and phrase boxes at the bottom of p. 12.

**Arbeitsbuch, Lektion 1** (Basistraining pages): do exercises 1–6, then the **Test** page. Check everything with the Arbeitsbuch answer key (*AB-LSCH* file) and note anything you got wrong.

items.q: It's 8:00 at work. Greet your manager, Frau Klein, formally.
Ask your neighbour, whom you call Sie, how he is.
Ask a friend how she is (full form, not Wie geht's).
Answer: you're fine, thanks, and ask back informally.
accept: Mir geht es gut, danke. Und dir?

items.q: Say goodbye at the end of an appointment at the Bürgeramt.
In German: Can you spell that, please?
Fill in sein: Das ___ mein Kollege Jan.
Make it informal (du): Woher kommen Sie und wie heißen Sie?
items.answer: Woher kommst du und wie heißt du?

items.q: In German: She comes from Switzerland, too.
items.answer: Sie kommt auch aus der Schweiz.

items.q: Which greeting do you use when you go to bed?

steps.title: Write about yourself
steps.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences introducing yourself to a new team at work: your name, where you come from, where you live now, and how you are today. Use ich bin / ich heiße / ich komme aus / ich wohne in.

steps.title: Speaking: meeting people
steps.prompt: Role-play: your first day at a new job. Greet colleagues (du and Sie), say your name, spell it, say where you come from, and ask them the same questions.
